To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a robust, fast and accurate method for multi-atlas segmentation.

the combination of the following factors leads to fast and accurate segmentation: 1) use of intensity differences instead of standard normal mutual information in registration, 2) selection of the best matching atlas based on registration accuracy, 3) segmentation via EM and 4) optimisation via graph-cuts.

(1) intensity normalised images and the intensity difference measure can be used in registration without compromising accuracy but leading to a threefold decrease in computation time, (2) a combination of the EM segmentation and graph cuts optimisation is a promising method for combining multi-atlass segmentation and intensity modelling, and (3) our optimised pipeline can be used for accurate, robust and fast segmentation of subcortical brain structures from brain MRI data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
optimisation of a segmentation pipeline for brain MRI.
the development and evaluation of a robust and efficient method for multi-atlas segmentation, which is based on the optimised combination of different components.
the development of an optimised pipeline that combines different methods for non-rigid registration, atlas selection and segmentation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed segmentation method is robust, fast and accurate.
the proposed method is accurate and fast, and can therefore be applied in clinical routine.
the proposed method is fast and robust, and can be used to produce high quality segmentation for a wide range of applications in neuroimaging research.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our pipeline is fast, robust and accurate.
the proposed pipeline is robust and fast, and it can be used for large-scale studies of brain MRI segmentation.
we have introduced a robust and efficient method for multi-atlas segmentation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the segmentation accuracy can be improved with a small increase in the computation time, and the segmentation speed can be improved without a decrease in the segmentation accuracy.
the proposed optimised pipeline is robust and accurate, fast and can be easily adapted for other brain structures and MRI modalities.
the combination of intensity modelling, multi-atlas segmentation, and optimised similarity measures and atlas selection can be used to generate fast and accurate segmentations of brain MRIs.
